newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close lower on Wall Street fall.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close lower on Wall Street fall.

text.p: French stocks closed lower on Monday after the French market tracked an early decline on Wall Street due to profit-taking.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished down 19 points, or 0.78 percent, at 2,406.10 after giving up an early advance that lifted it an all-time intraday high of 2,438.50 points earlier.
The CAC-40 January futures contract fell 17 points to 2,412.
Volume was a heavy 6.5 billion francs.
* Shares in oil firm Elf Aquitaine rose 1.96 percent to 520 francs, helped by the dollar's gains and an upgrade on the stock by U.S. investment firm Goldman Sachs.

* Eurotunnel shares closed up 5.8 percent at 7.30 francs after the Channel Tunnel operator reported a rise in passengers to 13 million in 1996 and said it hoped to finish negotiating details of a bank debt accord by March.
* LVMH closed down 3.61 percent at 1,495 francs. Traders cited profit-taking on its big recent gains.

* Rumours about changes in the ownership structure of the holding company of retailer Pinault-Printemps-Redoute drove the shares up 0.98 percent at 2,363 francs. There is talk state agency CDR may sell a 17 percent stake in Artemis, which controls Pinault-Printemps. CDR and Artemis declined comment.

* Shares in bank Credit Foncier slipped 0.16 percent to 63 francs. The chairman declared himself a hostage on Monday and broke off talks with unions as a staff siege at the troubled bank's headquarters dragged into a fourth day.

* Appliance manufacturer Moulinex reversed its early loss -- described by analysts as a knee-jerk reaction to the expected announcement on Friday of a capital increase -- and finished up 0.62 percent at 129.80 francs. Moulinex forecast a higher operating profit for 1996/97 in its prospectus.

* Shares in Thomson-CSF, the defense electronics arm of state-owned Thomson SA, fell 2.62 percent to 167.50 francs on concerns the French government may decide to privatise Thomson-CSF through the sale of shares at a discount.

The government has not yet announced how it plans to privatise Thomson-CSF, but brokers said a share sale looks more likely since the state's decision last month to scrap a prior plan to sell the entire Thomson group in one go.
* Drinks group Remy-Cointreau finished up 0.62 percent at 145.80 francs after reporting a rise in nine-month sales to 5.42 billion francs from 5.11 billion.
* "It's normal for the market to pause for breath," said a trader. The CAC index set four closing records last week.
Brokers said the market will probably trade cautiously ahead of U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony on the U.S. economy before the Senate on Tuesday.
They said Merrill Lynch's judgment that the Paris bourse was correctly valued now after catching up with other European stockmarkets also had a dampening effect.
